full_original_page:
# 859. Free Lie subalgebras in rational homotopy

**Area:** Rational homotopy theory
**Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL
**Last checked:** 2026-10-30

## Problem statement

Let $`X`$ be a simply connected finite CW complex. Give
```math
L_X=\bigoplus_{n\geq1}\pi_n(\Omega X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q
```
the graded Lie bracket induced by the Samelson product. Assume that $`L_X`$ has infinite total dimension over $`\mathbb Q`$; equivalently, $`X`$ is rationally hyperbolic.

Must $`L_X`$ contain a free graded Lie subalgebra on two generators? Explicitly, must there exist homogeneous $`u,v\in L_X`$ such that the homomorphism from the free graded Lie algebra over $`\mathbb Q`$ on generators of degrees $`|u|`$ and $`|v|`$, sending those generators to $`u,v`$, is injective?

No prescribed parity or equality of the generator degrees is required. This is the classical simply connected finite-complex Avramov-Félix conjecture. Broader versions for finite rational category or nonsimply connected spaces are not part of this entry.

## Application

The conjecture asks for a free algebraic structure inside the rational homotopy of every hyperbolic finite complex. It would clarify the structure underlying the already known exponential growth of rational homotopy groups.

## References

1. Martin Markl and Stefan Papadima, *Homotopy Lie algebras and fundamental groups via deformation theory*, Annales de l'Institut Fourier **42** (1992), 905–935. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.5802/aif.1315); [primary PDF](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.1315.pdf#page=5), printed p.908. Discovery source, also discussing a broader version.
2. Mark Grant, Gregory Lupton and John Oprea, *A mapping theorem for topological complexity*, Algebraic & Geometric Topology **15** (2015), 1643–1666. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2140/agt.2015.15.1643); [primary PDF](https://msp.org/agt/2015/15-3/agt-v15-n3-p10-p.pdf), Conjecture 5.1, printed p.1661.
3. Yves Félix and Stephen Halperin, *Rational homotopy via Sullivan models and enriched Lie algebras*, EMS Surveys in Mathematical Sciences **10** (2023), 101–122. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.4171/EMSS/67); [primary PDF](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/37046), §6.1, printed p.114.

## Status review


**Known cases:** The classical simply connected finite-complex Avramov-Felix conjecture is still explicitly retained in the 2023 survey. Additional topological-complexity assumptions give cases, but not an arbitrary rationally hyperbolic finite complex. Broader enriched-Lie conventions do not settle this subalgebra assertion.

**Remaining target:** Resolve the full Problem statement with its stated quantifiers and hypotheses; the restricted advances discussed here do not settle that target.
